explanation: The Act of 1807 outlawed the trade and not the institution, and many of its supporters expected the one to finish the other; it did not. What followed instead was a twenty-six-year apparatus — the Slave Trade Felony Act of 1811 making the overseas traffic a felony, the West Africa Squadron sent to suppress it, the Anti-Slavery Society founded in 1823, the Colonial Office rejecting colonial slave legislation as it arrived in London. 1833 is where that apparatus finally reached the thing itself. `precondition-of`: the first act made the second thinkable and did not make it happen.
